Papa Johns - The pizza is horrible but you can order online and they deliver to my office. I stopped using them because of their decision to cut back on Fry and his brethren's hours to avoid providing health benefits. I have since found they have many other despicable practices. At one point in my life I delivered pizzas so I know how hard the job is and what it does to your car. I'm not a socialist or a fiscal liberal but dammed if I am going to support this corporation. I use locally owned pizzerias now. I don't mind ordering by phone and the pizza is better.

Papa Johns offers online ordering and delivery to my office, but I think its pizza is horrible. I stopped using the chain after it reduced Fry’s hours, along with those of other employees, to avoid providing health benefits. Since then, I’ve learned about other practices I consider morally objectionable. I used to deliver pizzas, and the job is difficult; driving also wears out a delivery driver’s car. I’m not a socialist or a fiscal liberal, but I refuse to support Papa Johns. Now I order from locally owned pizzerias. Phone ordering is fine, and their pizza is better.

Hertz car rental. After they screwed up a simple insurance claim (RV hit my unoccupied, parked rental car, left their insurance info, their insurer denied the claim, Hertz shrugged and said "oh, well-- pay us $$$" instead of pushing it when the other driver was clearly at fault), I staged a one-woman boycott on them for 8 years. Next time I rented with them, they gave my car away less than an hour after my late plane landed-- when all travel was jacked up and delayed due to the new fluids ban. They didn't have another car available, at all-- I was lucky enough to be stranded in a town where I have family to come help me out. After I got home, I wrote them a nasty letter, to which they replied "Too bad." My blog post about their shitty customer service and how to reach an actual human being is still one of the most-found posts in my blog by people searching for "Hertz customer service real address." They hide their address so people can't complain directly.

If you’re considering Hertz—or searching online for a real person in customer service—here’s my experience.

Years ago, an RV hit my unoccupied Hertz rental car while it was parked. The driver left insurance information, but the insurer denied my claim. Hertz didn’t pursue it. Instead, they told me I was responsible for paying for the damage, even though the other driver appeared to be at fault. I boycotted Hertz for eight years.

When I finally rented from them again, my flight was delayed during the widespread confusion over the newly introduced fluids ban. Less than an hour after I arrived, Hertz had given away my reserved car. They had no replacement, so I was stranded in a town where, fortunately, family could help.

After I got home, I sent an angry letter. Hertz basically refused to help.

My blog post about Hertz’s service—and finding an actual human contact—remains one of my most-discovered pages, especially for searches about Hertz’s real customer-service address, which the company seems to hide to discourage direct complaints.
